Mixed Measures **__VERSION__** — a local-first desktop workspace for mixed-methods research: qualitative and quantitative data in one project, with shared participants, codes, and memos. Everything stays on your own computer — no account, no uploads, no telemetry.

**What's new in this release**

This release settles, in one go, the numbers an external review of Mixed Measures
questioned. Several results are now counted the way their method requires, so **a
figure you reported from an earlier version can differ** — each item below says where,
and the changelog's *Upgrade notes* list them all.

- 🔴 **The code-by-group comparison counts participants, not passages.** One talkative participant could make a code look significant: in a test with no real difference between groups, nearly half of 40 codes were starred. Each cell now counts the participants in the group who used the code, three or more groups take an exact test, and the p-values are adjusted across the codes tested with a discrete Holm correction, which can still find a difference at qualitative sample sizes. Expect fewer stars. The comparison also counts the open-text answers and linked documents you select.
- 🔴 **Reliability leaves interviewer turns out and counts a group of turns once.** Two coders who both left an interviewer's questions uncoded agreed on every one of them, which raised agreement without measuring it. A verdict now needs 18 passages coded by two or more people; below that the figure reads "too few to judge". The exported R script's Krippendorff's α now matches the app for complete data from three or more coders.
- 🔴 **Consensus decides a group of turns once,** and the update recomputes a consensus saved by an earlier version, so every tab agrees with the Reconciliation grid. Two codes now co-occur only where one coder applied both, so a disagreement no longer reads as a relationship — co-occurrence counts fall on projects coded by more than one person.
- 🔴 **The quantitative statistics match the standard packages.** A 2 × 2 cross-tabulation's chi-square no longer applies Yates's correction (χ² and Cramér's V rise, p falls); a group with one value is left out of the tests that need its spread, and says so; Mann–Whitney chooses its p as R, jamovi and JASP do; intervals over a variable group's pooled answers count each record once (usually wider); and an answer that differs from a scale label only in capitals or spaces counts under the label.
- 🔴 **Qualitative frequencies count what they say they count.** A code applied to an answer your project counts as no response no longer counts; "Unclear" and "Unsubstantive/Artifact" no longer show a share of the coded total (which could read 150%); and the co-occurrence matrix and the frequency files count exactly what you selected. The Frequencies CSV is now the Descriptives summary table, with new columns — a script that read the old file needs updating.
- 🔴 **A participant filter reads every kind of source one way.** It narrowed interview turns and survey answers but counted every document and observation clip; a document now counts only when it is linked to a selected participant, and clips are left out while a filter is on. The filter also stays on until you change it, and values no participant holds together no longer show the whole project.
- **Blind coding reaches the files.** While your colleagues' coding is hidden, the Export dialog's coding files, the Text Coding export, Cross-analysis, the Quote Board and the analysis page's passage lists hold only your own coding. Before, a file exported while blind held every coder's work.
- **The exports hold what the screen holds.** The Cross-analysis CSV had never applied the panel's filters; the analysis page's Segments, Source Data and Co-occurrence CSVs now hold the selection on screen; and a file exported under a participant filter says so on its first line. Several files gained columns or a first line — the changelog lists them.
- **Bigger projects open.** On a project with several million codings, the project list and a project's Overview failed while the app worked out who had coded it; that now takes milliseconds. The Qualitative analysis page loads on a large survey project, and the Quote Board opens with a thousand quotes or more. (On the very largest test project the coding pages still time out; the changelog says where.)
- **A withdrawal reaches further.** It now removes a person's words from turns that were merged and later separated again; a withdrawal made in a colleague's copy stops the merge instead of disappearing into it; and a transcript no longer brings a withdrawn person back under a name the project knew them by. The changelog names what it still does not reach.
- **And smaller fixes.** Three tables can be sorted from the keyboard, numbers on heatmap and cross-tab cells are readable on every cell colour, the chart options show only each option's name, the Data Quality link after an import opens the Data Quality tab, and the Text Coding export keeps its `.csv` ending with a long project name.

<!-- Update the next paragraph at every cut: the cut-off is the last release that used the PREVIOUS .mmproject format, not a fixed number. 1.5.4 introduced format 7; 1.5.5 to 1.6.0 write the same format. 1.5.8 added coder identities and the withdrawal record to it, and 1.6.0 the names a withdrawal remembers; older versions ignore what they do not know. -->
- 🔴 **Read this before you share a project file.** **Project files saved by __VERSION__ do not open in 1.5.3 or earlier** — 1.5.4 changed how a project file stores your data, and an older version refuses such a file and says so rather than importing a project that appears to be empty. **Files from older versions still open here as normal.** 1.5.4 and later write the same format, **but an older version ignores what a later one adds and leaves it out of anything it exports: versions before 1.5.8 ignore who each coder is and what a withdrawal removed, and 1.5.8 ignores the names a __VERSION__ withdrawal remembers and does not stop a merge that would keep someone withdrawn.** If you are working with a colleague, update together before you exchange `.mmproject` files, above all for a project from which someone has withdrawn. **A backup (`.mmbackup`) made by __VERSION__ is refused by 1.5.8**, which says so and changes nothing.
- **If your team shared a project before 1.5.8, the first merge after updating may ask about people you already work with.** Each computer gave its coders an identity of its own when it updated, so Merge's *Confirm coders* step can know a colleague here only by name, and waits for your answer. Choose *Map to* their name only for the same person, and *Add as new coder* for anyone else: a wrong answer makes two people one coder, or one person two. This version does not yet remember a *Map to* answer, so the question comes back at each merge of that colleague's copy.
- 🔴 **This update changes your database, and takes a copy first.** The first launch adds one index to your codings and queues the consensus saved on grouped turns for a recompute — and, coming from a version before 1.5.8, also makes that version's changes (every coder given an identity, a place for the record of what a withdrawal removed, formulas that compare a variable with a quoted answer marked out of date). The copy needs free disk space about the size of your database. The startup screen says it is updating your data; keep Mixed Measures open until it finishes — a large project can take several minutes. If the update fails, it is undone completely and your previous version can still open the data. **Once __VERSION__ has updated your data, do not go back to an earlier version:** 1.5.8 refuses to open it and changes nothing, and 1.5.7 and earlier cannot open it either and replace one of the copies taken before the update at each attempt, until none from before it is left. If something goes wrong, install __VERSION__ again. **If your project matters to you, copy your data folder somewhere of your own before upgrading:** a copy you control is the only one the app's own rotation can never reach. Full details in the [changelog](https://github.com/__REPO__/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Which file should I download?

Pick the one for your computer and click it:

- **macOS** (Apple Silicon — M1 or later) → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-mac-arm64.dmg)**
- **Windows** → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-win-x64.exe](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-win-x64.exe)**
- **Linux** → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-linux-x86_64.AppImage](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-linux-x86_64.AppImage)**

> **Not sure if your Mac is Apple Silicon?** Click the Apple menu (top-left) → **About This Mac**. If the **Chip** line says "Apple M1" (or any later Apple chip), this is the right file. Older Intel Macs aren't supported in this release.

<!-- Requirements: re-check at every cut. macOS from electron/package.json build.mac.minimumSystemVersion (the release's "macOS floor" step proves it against every binary); Windows from Electron's own README "Platform support"; Linux from the AppImage's highest GLIBC_ symbol version (2.38 measured on v1.5.5 — the frozen backend's libraries, collected on the ubuntu-24.04 runner). -->
**What it runs on**

- **macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later**, on Apple Silicon. A Mac on an older version is not offered this update; every Apple Silicon Mac can be updated to macOS 14.
- **Windows 10 or 11**, 64-bit.
- **Linux**, 64-bit, with glibc 2.38 or newer — Ubuntu 24.04 or later, for example.

You can **ignore the other files** in the Assets list below (the `.blockmap` and `.yml` files) — the app uses those for updates; you don't need to download them.

## First launch

The Windows and macOS installers are signed (and notarized on macOS), so the verified publisher is **George Chavez**; the Linux AppImage is not signed. Because the app is new and independent, your system may show a one-time prompt the first time you open it. This is normal and fades as more people install it — it is not a sign that anything is wrong.

- **macOS:** drag Mixed Measures to your Applications folder. If it doesn't open on a double-click, right-click it → **Open**.
- **Windows:** if you see "Windows protected your PC," click **More info → Run anyway** (you'll see *George Chavez* listed as the publisher).

See the [README](https://github.com/__REPO__#readme) to get started.
